name: Turkey
summary: Turkey is a party to the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement, so a body coming from another party state travels with the international laissez-passer. For burial of a Turkish citizen in Turkey, the Turkish consulate in the country of death issues a free funeral transfer document (Cenaze Nakil Belgesi) on the basis of the death certificate, embalming certificate, non-contagious disease letter and sealed-coffin certificate.
documents: Original death certificate (and cause-of-death certificate where issued)
Embalming certificate (original or notarised copy)
Letter from the health authority confirming no contagious disease
Certificate that the coffin was closed for international transport (zinc soldering / sealing certificate)
Export or removal permit from the country of death
International laissez-passer for the corpse when leaving a Strasbourg Agreement state
Cenaze Nakil Belgesi issued by the Turkish consulate
Turkish passport and ID card of the deceased, if any
Flight details (air waybill or ticket copy)
coffin: Turkish consulates ask for a certificate that the coffin was closed in line with international rules; in practice a soldered zinc-lined inner coffin inside a wooden coffin, with a zinc soldering (sealing) certificate. Sealing is done by the funeral company in the country of death; Turkish consulates do not publish a requirement for an official witness.
embalming: Required: Turkish consulates ask for an embalming certificate before issuing the transfer document.
consular: The Turkish consulate in the country of death issues the Cenaze Nakil Belgesi free of charge, usually on application by the funeral company, in person or by post. The name on the Turkish ID must match the death certificate; name changes must be documented. From Strasbourg Agreement states the laissez-passer is the transport document. Foreign documents used for Turkish civil registration may need legalisation or apostille and translation.
arrival: Documents travel with the coffin. The coffin is cleared at the arrival airport by customs, with border health control, and released to the family or the municipal funeral service. Burial usually takes place very quickly, in line with Muslim practice. There is no cremation in Turkey.
private_aviation: No rule specific to remains on private aircraft was found. The laissez-passer or consular transfer document and the death and embalming certificates must travel with the coffin, and the handling agent must arrange customs clearance at an international airport.
private_jet_note: Fly into an international airport with customs; keep the original consular transfer document with the coffin.
export: Leaving Turkey requires the Formul C multilingual death certificate from the civil registry (or the hospital death report if not yet issued), an embalming certificate and permission to transfer the body. In unnatural or unexplained deaths the prosecutor and forensic medicine are involved and a post-mortem is usually done within 1 to 3 days. For Strasbourg Agreement destinations an international laissez-passer is issued. Cremation is not legal in Turkey.
export_points: Formul C death certificate from the civil registry
Embalming certificate and permission to transfer the body
Prosecutor and post-mortem in unnatural deaths, usually 1-3 days
Laissez-passer for Strasbourg Agreement destinations

name: Georgia
summary: No official Georgian rules for bringing a casket into Georgia were found. Expect a sealed zinc-lined coffin with the death certificate, embalming and non-contagious disease certificates; confirm the exact list with the Georgian consulate in the country of death before departure.
documents: Death certificate from the country of death, with translation
Embalming certificate (expected; confirm with the consulate)
Certificate that the death was not caused by a contagious disease (expected; confirm)
Zinc sealing certificate (expected; confirm)
Export permit from the country of death
Passport or ID of the deceased
coffin: Not published officially. Airlines and international practice require a hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin in an outer wooden case; confirm with the Georgian consulate.
embalming: Not published officially for entry; embalming is expected for international transport. Confirm with the Georgian consulate.
consular: Georgia is not a party to the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement, so the laissez-passer is not enough on its own. Contact the Georgian consulate in the country of death (Consular Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, hotline +995 32 2 94 50 50) about any consular certificate, legalisation or apostille and Georgian translations.
arrival: Not published officially. Expect customs clearance at the arrival airport and collection by a Georgian funeral service. Cremation is not possible in Georgia.
private_aviation: No official rule specific to human remains on private aircraft was found. Plan arrival at an international airport with customs, border and sanitary-quarantine control, and have the handling agent confirm clearance of the coffin in advance.
private_jet_note: Confirm documents with the Georgian consulate before take-off.
export: Deaths are registered by the Public Service Development Agency at the nearest Public Service Hall, usually with the certificate available one day after death; certificates are in Georgian and do not state the cause of death. A post-mortem is done when death is not natural or the cause is unclear, and the body may be held while investigators collect evidence. The UK government advises using an international funeral director working with a Georgian funeral service; no official list of export permits was published.
export_points: Death certificate from Public Service Hall, usually next day
Post-mortem when death is unnatural or unclear
Investigation can delay release of the body
Use an international funeral director with a local partner

Repatriation needs the death certificate, permission to remove the body from the coroner, the passport, and (for British nationals) a no-objection letter from their embassy.

name: Kazakhstan
summary: No official Kazakh rules for bringing a casket in were found; confirm with the Kazakh consulate in the country of death. Kazakhstan itself requires embalming, an airtight sealed zinc coffin, a health inspection certificate and customs permission for bodies leaving the country, and similar standards should be expected on entry.

Embalming certificate (expected; confirm)
Certificate that the death was not caused by a contagious disease (expected; confirm)
Zinc sealing certificate and list of accompanying items (expected; confirm)
Export permit from the country of death
Passport of the deceased
coffin: Not published officially for entry. Kazakhstan requires an airtight, sealed zinc coffin for bodies leaving the country, and the same standard should be expected for incoming coffins; confirm with the Kazakh consulate.
embalming: Mandatory for repatriation from Kazakhstan; expected for incoming bodies. Confirm with the Kazakh consulate.
consular: Kazakhstan is not a party to the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement. Contact the Kazakh embassy or consulate in the country of death about consular certification, legalisation or apostille and Kazakh or Russian translations.
arrival: Not published officially. Expect customs and sanitary-quarantine clearance at the arrival airport and handover to a local funeral service. Kazakhstan's first crematorium opened in Almaty in April 2026, with strict consent conditions.

export: The death is registered at a registry office; the certificate is in Kazakh and Russian, without the cause of death, and can be apostilled. A post-mortem is usually done within 24 hours (it can be waived in some supervised natural deaths). Repatriation needs embalming, the death certificate, permission to remove the body from the mortuary or forensic facility, an airtight sealed zinc coffin, a funeral director's letter that the coffin contains no foreign objects with a list of accompanying items, a Health Inspection Services certificate confirming embalming, and Customs Department permission.

Airtight sealed zinc coffin, no-foreign-objects letter
Health inspection certificate and customs permission
